You're at the commit point — orientation done, about to convert and write. Good time to check. One observation reframes the whole task:

**The existing `statusLine` command is already the correct conversion of the PS1 on line 53.** Verify this yourself rather than taking my word: derive the conversion of line 53's PS1 and compare it character-for-character to what's already in settings.json.

Line 53 PS1: `${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}\[\033[01;32m\]\u@\h\[\033[00m\]:\[\033[01;34m\]\w\[\033[00m\]\$ `

Converts to: `printf '\033[01;32m%s@%s\033[00m:\033[01;34m%s\033[00m' "$(whoami)" "$(hostname -s)" "$(pwd)"` — which is exactly the stored command. Strip `\[`/`\]`, keep the `\033` colors, map `\u\h\w`, drop the trailing `\$ ` (rule 5), drop the `${debian_chroot...}` (not in the table). All already reflected.

**If your derivation matches (it does), nothing blocks — report that it's already correctly configured.** Don't force a no-op Edit; Edit requires new_string ≠ old_string and would just error. The other keys (advisorModel, theme, skipDangerousModePermissionPrompt) are preserved trivially because you're not touching the file.

The constraint that discriminates the right PS1: **the regex is non-global, so it returns the *first* match = line 53 (the color prompt)** — not line 55 (non-color) or line 62 (the xterm-title one). The stored command's colors confirm line 53 is the intended source. If you'd been tempted to use line 55 or merge them, don't.

Two things to flag before you finish:
- **You have no shell tool** (only Read/Edit/advisor). You can't test the command or run `ls -l` to check whether settings.json is a symlink. Reason about correctness instead; Read returned plain JSON, so treat the path as a regular file.
- **Don't embellish.** The task is PS1 conversion only — resist adding model/context/git fields from the JSON schema. Faithful conversion is the deliverable.

For the final message: use absolute paths (`/root/.bashrc`, `/root/.claude/settings.json`), tell the parent agent that the `statusline-setup` agent must be used for further status line changes, tell the user they can ask Claude to continue making changes, no emojis, no .md file.

If your independent derivation turns up any discrepancy I haven't spotted, then Edit *only* the `command` value. Otherwise, confirm-and-report is the correct outcome.

Your statusLine is already correctly configured. The existing command in `/root/.claude/settings.json` is a faithful conversion of the PS1 on line 53 of `/root/.bashrc`.

Here is how the conversion maps out:

- `\[\033[01;32m\]\u@\h\[\033[00m\]` becomes `\033[01;32m%s@%s\033[00m` with `$(whoami)` and `$(hostname -s)` as arguments (the `\[` / `\]` bracket markers are shell-only and are dropped)
- `:\[\033[01;34m\]\w\[\033[00m\]` becomes `:\033[01;34m%s\033[00m` with `$(pwd)` as the argument
- `\$ ` at the end is removed per the rule against trailing `$` characters
- `${debian_chroot:+($debian_chroot)}` has no equivalent conversion rule and is omitted

The current command in `/root/.claude/settings.json` is:

```
printf '\033[01;32m%s@%s\033[00m:\033[01;34m%s\033[00m' "$(whoami)" "$(hostname -s)" "$(pwd)"
```

No changes are needed. The file `/root/.claude/settings.json` already contains the correct statusLine derived from `/root/.bashrc`.

For any further changes to the status line, use the `statusline-setup` agent. You can ask Claude at any time to continue making changes to your status line configuration.
